title.value: STATIC PREDICTION OF RUNTIME ERRORS BY LEARNING TO EXECUTE PROGRAMS WITH EXTERNAL RESOURCE DESCRIPTIONS
title.justification: The title represents the core focus of the paper, which is predicting runtime errors in programs using machine learning models that consider the description of external resources.
title.quote: S TATIC P REDICTION OF RUNTIME E RRORS BY L EARNING TO E XECUTE P ROGRAMS WITH E XTERNAL R ESOURCE D ESCRIPTIONS

extractions.description: The paper focuses on predicting runtime errors in programs before they are executed by developing a new dataset and machine learning models that learn to execute programs with descriptions of external resources.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving the prediction of runtime errors in software development, which is not directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We investigate applying neural machine learning methods to the static analysis of source code for early prediction of runtime errors.

primary_category.justification: The paper is centered around software development and error prediction, which do not directly address any Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development goals.
primary_category.quote: Here, we introduce a competitive programming dataset and task for predicting runtime errors, which has real-world value for software developers, but is not connected to sustainability topics.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes in the paper that relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: The task is difficult-yet-approachable and has real-world value for software developers, but it does not pertain to climate or ecological themes.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper doesn't address any specific sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as it is focused on software development issues.
primary_sub_category.quote: We present a practical and difficult-yet-approachable challenge problem related to learning program execution behavior.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not cover any additional sustainable development sub-categories as its central theme is unrelated to these areas.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The models support the complexity of competition code and demonstrate the capabilities of interpreter-inspired models.

applications.value: Identifying and predicting runtime errors in Python programs using static analysis and machine learning models.
applications.justification: This application is the central contribution of the paper, aiming to help software developers by predicting errors without executing the code.
applications.quote: We introduce the runtime error prediction task and a large accompanying dataset, providing runtime error annotations for millions of competition Python programs.

new_primary_category.justification: A new category is suggested as the paper focuses on enhancing software development tools, specifically in predicting runtime errors, which is not covered by existing sustainability categories.
new_primary_category.quote: We demonstrate promising new capabilities of interpreter-inspired machine learning models for code.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category of Runtime Error Prediction under Software Development Improvement suits the paper as it specifically targets improvements in predicting software errors.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We introduce a competitive programming dataset and task for predicting runtime errors, which we show is difficult for generic models like Transformers.
